errors.text: The proposed rapid treatment at 800–900°C replaces the required hydrogen de-binding and prolonged vacuum sintering at 1400°C; it is unlikely to complete in-situ alloying and densification of refractory powders.

The hypothesis seeks near-total oxygen exclusion and imposes a >50 ppm falsification threshold, whereas the target mechanism deliberately retains approximately 1.0 wt.% oxygen for interstitial strengthening.
It omits the sequential hydride decomposition governed by hydride formation enthalpies and the titanium-sponge oxygen getter.
It omits water quenching from 1500°C, the key control used to suppress alpha-HCP formation and retain metastable beta-BCC.
The claimed high-strain-rate suppression of alpha-HCP precipitation is not supported by the cited evidence.
The proposed Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V/Ti/Zr chemistry does not reconstruct the equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr hydride-based ink system.
The prediction of an elevated ductile-to-brittle transition temperature is directionally inconsistent with the goal of mitigating oxygen-induced embrittlement.
